failure_patterns.pattern: incomplete_tool_action_or_persistence: Some trajectories omitted required actions or failed to save results; one produced no executable plan.

rejected_edits.content: Descriptions such as “last-minute” or “weekend getaway” do not specify flight departure dates, and occasions or dietary needs (for example, a birthday or gluten-free request) do not specify a restaurant city. Ask for the actual missing mandatory value rather than substituting a default.
rejected_edits.target: Before searching, match each required tool field to an explicit value in the full conversation; related context does not automatically satisfy that field.

rejected_edits.content: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list or widen an exact value. For minimum-only or maximum-only criteria, use the documented scale bounds for the other endpoint: for example, on a 0–5 hotel or restaurant rating scale, encode “at least x” as `[x, 5]` and “at most x” as `[0, x]`. Follow the schema for other bounds and do not invent endpoints.
rejected_edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
